domBefore.bodyText: Map 🌐 Fact Finder LV.1 Milestone 🔬 Part 1: Why Wet Floors Are Slippery Step 1 of 3 Science LV.1 MODE: 🔤 Vocab Focus 🔬 Grammar X-Ray 🔊 Listen to whole text 🎧 Listen to this part KEY COLLOCATIONS & CHUNKS (11) Interactive Word Bank slippery layer shoe soles rubber soles warning signs reduces friction stays balanced smooth tiles wet tiles school corridor strong grip wet floors SCIENCE & NATURE GLOSSARY Key Terms (Click any term or word for full dictionary) Friction: A physical force that prevents surfaces from sliding easily. Grip: The hold between shoe soles and the floor surface. Rubber Soles: Bottom of shoes made of rubber for high traction. Smooth Tiles: Floor surface that becomes very slippery when wet. Slippery Layer: A thin film of water that reduces friction. Warning Sign: A bright yellow sign that alerts people to walk slowly. Balance: Staying steady on your feet without falling over. Surface: The flat top or outer boundary of an object or floor. 📖 PARAGRAPH 1: WHY WET FLOORS ARE SLIPPERY Why do people slip on wet floors? The answer is a science force called friction. Friction is the grip between two surfaces that stops things from sliding. When a student walks on dry tiles, shoe soles grip the floor firmly and the student stays balanced. But water on smooth tiles creates a thin slippery layer. This water layer reduces friction, so shoes slide easily. CHECK QUESTIONS (2 QUESTIONS) What is the science force that stops objects from sliding? A Friction B Gravity C Wind force Why did Jake not slip while walking down the dry corridor? A His rubber shoes created high friction with dry floor B He walked with closed eyes C He was holding the wall Next: Part 2 ▶ UPGRADE PLAN
